title: Eggs Benedict

items.raw: 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice, plus more to taste
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, melted and hot
Pinch of salt and a pinch of cayenne
Chopped chives and paprika, to finish

steps.text: Blend the yolks, lemon juice, salt, and cayenne for 5 seconds. With the blender running, pour in the hot melted butter in a very thin stream until thick and creamy. Taste for lemon and salt. Keep warm in a small bowl set over warm (not simmering) water and use within 1 hour; discard what is left after that.

Whisk the yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl set over barely simmering water, whisking constantly, until thick, pale, and 160°F on an instant-read thermometer — that is what makes the yolks safe. Do not let them go past about 170°F or they will scramble. Remove from the heat and whisk in the melted butter a spoonful at a time.
Fill a wide saucepan with 3 inches of water, add the vinegar, and bring to a bare simmer — small bubbles on the bottom, the surface barely moving.

Crack each egg into a small cup. Stir the water gently, then slide the eggs in one at a time. Poach 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still soft. Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on a towel.
Meanwhile, brown the Canadian bacon in a skillet 1 to 2 minutes per side. Toast and butter the English muffins.
Top each muffin half with a slice of bacon and a poached egg. Spoon over a generous amount of hollandaise and finish with chives and a pinch of paprika. Serve at once.

notes.label: Fresh eggs poach best
notes.text: older eggs have runny whites that feather into the water. Straining the egg in a fine sieve for a few seconds before poaching removes the loose white.

notes.label: Poach ahead
notes.text: poach eggs up to a day ahead, chill in ice water, and refrigerate. Reheat in hot water for 60 seconds just before serving.

notes.label: If the hollandaise breaks
notes.text: whisk a teaspoon of hot water into a fresh yolk, then slowly whisk the broken sauce into it.

notes.label: Raw-egg caution
notes.text: blender hollandaise does not fully cook the yolks. Use pasteurized eggs for anyone pregnant, elderly, or immune-compromised.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — the classic with Canadian bacon and hollandaise. Who makes it, and for what — Christmas morning, Mother’s Day, a birthday brunch? Tell me if the family version uses ham, smoked salmon, or spinach instead.
